transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-07
- Start time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Rachel (CISO - Elysium), Mark (Head of Platform), Sara (DevOps), Tom (Procurement)

[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, with Priya who will be our SE, and Liam on CSM. you all?
[00:00:10] Rachel: hi, Rachel Li, CISO at Elysium. Mark, Sara and Tom here. thanks for making time.
[00:00:20] Jordan: awesome. goal for today is to walk through security posture and make sure we cover SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. then we'll map that to hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:00:35] Priya: quick note, i'll drop in technical details and network stuff when we talk about VPC/on-prem.

[00:02:15] Mark: to kick off, high level on our side - we run a hybrid infra: prod workloads in GCP, some sensitive PHI-ish pipelines in a colo that has strict access controls. we're evaluating Redwood because we want LLM features but need to ensure compliance.
[00:02:30] Sara: main ask: no customer data should be retained in hosted unless we have encryption + retention policy that meets HIPAA-like constraints. we're looking at both dedicated and private. timeline is Q1 pilot, production by Q3.

[00:04:05] Jordan: understood. from a compliance perspective, Redwood's hosted offering is SOC 2 Type II audited and we maintain ISO 27001 summary—i'll share the reports. for PHI workloads we typically recommend Dedicated or Private depending on residency and contractual needs.
[00:04:20] Rachel: can you clarify what 'hosted' means for data at rest and in transit? where keys live?
[00:04:28] Priya: sure. hosted encrypts data in transit with TLS 1.2/1.3 and at rest using AES-256. by default keys are managed by Redwood KMS, but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) in Dedicated and Private via KMS/HSM integration. for SSO we support SAML and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning.
[00:04:45] Mark: okay CMK support good. how granular is RBAC? we need least-privilege down to environment/model level and ability to rotate keys without downtime.
[00:04:55] Priya: RBAC supports org>project>environment scopes, roles for admin/developer/auditor, and per-route model permissions are possible via policy tags. key rotation is supported; with CMK we orchestrate rotation with minimal impact to running workloads. for Dedicated we can provide full control over key lifecycle if needed.

[00:07:10] Rachel: audit logs - do you provide immutable logs, retention policies, and export to our SIEM? we need to ingest to Splunk/BigQuery and keep logs for at least 2 years for some audits.
[00:07:20] Jordan: yes, audit logs are available. hosted includes 90 days by default, extended retention is an add-on. we stream logs to customer endpoints — S3/GCS/Splunk/BigQuery. We can arrange long-term retention for enterprise agreements.
[00:07:35] Sara: when you say 'stream' are these syslogs or structured events with user, model, request-id, tokens?
[00:07:42] Priya: structured events; they include request metadata (request-id, user, model version, route, token counts, latency), and admin actions are logged with actor identity. we can include raw transcripts but that's opt-in and can be disabled.

[00:10:00] Mark: regulatory question — ISO and SOC attestations ok, but what about data residency? we need EU-only processing for some customers. can hosted guarantee that?
[00:10:10] Jordan: hosted can be regionally isolated; we run in multiple regions and can pin your org to EU region for processing. for strict EU data residency contractual clauses we recommend Dedicated or Private to guarantee physical isolation.

[00:12:55] Rachel: SSO / identity - we need SAML v2 support, MFA enforcement via IdP, SCIM for provisioning and ability to enforce session length. what does Redwood support today?
[00:13:05] Priya: SAML 2.0 and OIDC supported, integrates with Okta/Azure AD/Google. SCIM provisioning supported. You can enforce SSO-only policies and session durations. We also support role mapping from IdP groups to Redwood roles.

[00:15:30] Sara: about private deployments — if we go private on-prem, do you provide the control plane or is it fully customer-managed?
[00:15:38] Priya: Private can be deployed in two modes: customer-managed control plane (air-gapped option) or Redwood-managed control plane in your VPC. For air-gapped, you operate the control plane and we provide the install artifacts, operators. For VPC-managed, we run the control plane but network egress is restricted.
[00:15:55] Mark: for our security team, we also want to review the install manifests and least-privilege IAM roles.
[00:16:00] Priya: absolutely, we'll share those artifacts. Jordan will send the onboarding checklist and install guide.

[00:18:20] Rachel: encryption at rest for Private - is there an option for on-prem HSM?
[00:18:26] Priya: yes, HSM/KMS integrations supported. For on-prem you can bring-your-own-HSM and Redwood will plug into it. Hosted also supports customer-managed keys in cloud KMS via blind wrap and envelope encryption.

[00:21:05] Mark: A concern: model caching and KV caches - does any user-level data persist in caches that could be read by other tenants? we need tenant isolation.
[00:21:15] Priya: isolation is per-tenant. KV cache is scoped to the instance/project and not shared. For hosted multi-tenant, we logical-isolate resources; Dedicated gives dedicated GPU pools and stronger isolation. Private gives physical isolation. We'll share architecture diagrams.

[00:24:00] Rachel: retention policy controls — can we set retention per dataset or per route, and do you support automatic deletion and rekeying?
[00:24:10] Priya: yes, retention is configurable per project/route. We offer TTL-based deletion, manual purge, and re-encryption when keys are rotated. For strict deletion requirements we can provide audit evidence of deletion.

[00:27:30] Tom: procurement question - what does the procurement and legal process look like for Dedicated vs Private?
[00:27:38] Jordan: typically Dedicated requires a reserved capacity contract with monthly/annual commitments, Private is an enterprise license + support. We have standard enterprise terms with SOC/ISO addendums, DPAs, and specific clauses for data residency. procurement timeline usually 4-8 weeks once scope agreed.

[00:30:00] Sara: about backups — are model checkpoints or caching snapshots stored and how long by default? we want to ensure model artifacts are covered by our retention and access policies.
[00:30:10] Priya: model artifacts are versioned; backups for inference runtime are managed by Redwood with configurable retention. For Dedicated/Private, customers can control backup location and retention.

[00:32:45] Mark: logging integrity — can logs be tamper-evident? we currently use append-only logs with integrity checks.
[00:32:52] Priya: we can support write-once storage options and signed log exports to provide tamper evidence. We'll document the approach used.

[00:35:05] Rachel: breach notification and incident response — what's SLA and can we get runbooks?
[00:35:12] Jordan: incident response includes 24/7 security on-call for enterprise customers. we provide incident playbooks and RTO/RPO depending on deployment. we'll include breach notification timelines in the DPA.

[00:36:50] Sara: about least-privileged network - can Redwood accept peered VPC connections and private peering?
[00:36:58] Priya: yes, we support VPC peering, PrivateLink equivalents, and direct connect options for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be configured with customer VPN/peering for secure egress.

[00:39:20] Mark: any known gaps we should be aware of?
[00:39:25] Jordan: short answer, hosted's default retention and key ownership are our notable differences — hosted manages keys by default and retention is 90 days; for strict contractual or HIPAA-level controls we recommend Dedicated or Private. Also air-gapped on-prem requires more Ops from customer side.

[00:41:05] Rachel: cool. would be great to get the SOC 2 Type II, ISO summary, network diagrams, VPC onboarding doc, and the Dedicated pricing sheet.
[00:41:15] Jordan: will send: SOC2 + ISO by 11/10, VPC onboarding + install manifests by 11/12, Dedicated pricing and sample SOW for procurement by 11/16. Priya will scope a short benchmark for latency/cost.

[00:43:10] Tom: procurement has a standard question on insurance and indemnity - we'll include in our procurement list.
[00:43:20] Jordan: noted, Jordan will loop in legal and share their standard enterprise terms and cyber insurance details.

[00:44:30] Jordan: recap of next steps and action items... thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the pricing call.
[00:44:45] Rachel: thanks, talk soon.
[00:44:50] End of call
